mission: AI Impacts tries to improve our understanding of what human-level AI will do to the world. It is best known for the Expert Survey on Progress in AI, the largest and longest-running survey of AI researchers about timelines and risks. It also maintains a wiki and blog organising evidence on AI forecasting and risk.

key_work.title: Advanced AI according to 1,580 researchers: uncertain, unsafe, and sooner than we thought (2024 ESPAI)
key_work.plain_summary: Results of the 2024 Expert Survey on Progress in AI, asking researchers who publish at top AI venues how fast AI will advance and how good or bad its impacts may be.

key_work.title: Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI (2023 ESPAI)
key_work.plain_summary: Surveyed 2,778 AI researchers: most expect major milestones sooner than earlier surveys did, and many put non-trivial odds on extremely bad outcomes.

key_work.title: When Will AI Exceed Human Performance? Evidence from AI Experts (2016 ESPAI)
key_work.plain_summary: The first big AI-researcher survey on timelines, which became a widely cited reference point for when AI might match humans.

key_work.title: AI Impacts Wiki
key_work.plain_summary: An organised, continually revised collection of evidence and arguments on AI timelines, takeoff speed and risk.

warnings.text: Many AI researchers themselves assign meaningful probability to extremely bad outcomes from advanced AI, including human extinction.
Expert expectations for human-level AI have been moving earlier.
Public discussion of AI's long-term impacts is fragmented and of limited credibility.

recommendations.text: Base AI decisions on systematic evidence — surveys, trend data, historical analogies — rather than anecdote.
Identify and openly track disagreements about AI timelines and risks.
Take slowing down AI development seriously as an option (Katja Grace's writing on coordination).
